meta.title: Dev Workflow
meta.description: Development-workflow gatekeeper: skill-injected conventions, commit-message and doc-sync checks, and a git-guard for destructive git commands.

command.toggle.description: Turn the development-workflow gatekeeper on or off.
command.toggle.usage: Usage: /dev-workflow on | off | status | check. With no argument it reports the current state.
command.toggle.unknown: Unknown subcommand "{input}". Use on, off, status, or check.
command.toggle.status.on: dev-workflow is on. Conventions stay resident as a short summary; details are read on demand.
command.toggle.status.off: dev-workflow is off. Nothing is injected and nothing is checked.
command.toggle.status.never: No check has run in this session yet.
command.toggle.check.header: Development-workflow check of the working tree:
command.guard.dangerous_warning: This command does something that cannot be undone: {pattern}.
command.guard.confirm_required: Check the target before approving. If it is not the one you meant, reject.
command.guard.denied: Run it deliberately outside the plugin, or relax `commandGuard.dangerousShell` in configuration.
tool.check_commit_message.description: Validate a commit message against Conventional Commits.
tool.check_commit_message.param.message: Full commit message: subject line, optional body, optional footer.
tool.check_commit_message.param.files: Repository-relative paths this commit touches. Used to note a commit that spans several modules.
tool.check_commit_message.error.empty: The commit message is empty. Write a subject such as `feat(parser): reject empty input`.
tool.check_commit_message.error.missing_: The commit message has no type prefix.
tool.check_commit_message.hint.format: Expected `<type>(<scope>): <subject>`, for example `fix(git-guard): deny force push without confirmation`.
tool.check_commit_message.error.breaking: The `!` marker promises a breaking change, but no `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer explains it. Add a line starting with `BREAKING CHANGE: ` and say what breaks.
tool.check_commit_message.error.changelo: A `feat` commit must add a `{changelog}` entry under `[Unreleased]`. Add one line saying what the feature does.
tool.check_commit_message.warn.subject_l: The subject is {length} characters; Conventional Commits asks for {max} or fewer. Move the detail into the body.
tool.check_commit_message.warn.trailing_: The subject ends with a period. Conventional Commits leaves it off.
tool.check_commit_message.warn.body_widt: A body line is {length} characters; the specification wraps at {max}. Wrap it so the message reads in a narrow terminal.
tool.check_commit_message.warn.multiple_: This commit spans several modules ({modules}). If those changes answer different questions, split them into separate commits.
tool.check_commit_message.warn.missing_s: This change touches only {module}; name it in the scope: `<type>({module}): <subject>`.
tool.check_commit_message.error.missing_: This repository requires a scope, but the subject has none. Name the area: `<type>(<scope>): <subject>`.
tool.check_commit_message.ok: The commit message follows Conventional Commits.
tool.check_doc_sync.description: Check whether documentation was updated together with the code it describes.
tool.check_doc_sync.param.files: Repository-relative paths to check. Omit to read the working tree with `git status`.
tool.check_doc_sync.error.mirror: These files are kept in step with each other and only some of them changed. Changed: {changed}. Missing: {missing}.
tool.check_doc_sync.warn.no_document: {count} code file(s) changed with no documentation update — for example {example}. Add or update a file under {docsDir} if the change is user-visible or architectural.
tool.check_doc_sync.warn.changelog: {changelog} has no `[Unreleased]` entry for this change. Add one line saying what changed.
tool.check_doc_sync.warn.readme_on_confi: This change edits {files}, which configure the whole project, and no file listed in `docs.readme` changed with it. Say what the configuration change means for a reader.
tool.check_doc_sync.ok: Documentation and code are in sync.
error.not_a_git_repository: This is not a git repository.
error.git_not_available: git was not found on PATH.
error.cancelled: The git command was cancelled before it finished.
security.guard.force_push: A force push rewrites remote history and can discard other people's commits.
security.guard.hard_reset: A hard reset discards uncommitted work permanently.
security.guard.clean_force: git clean -f deletes untracked files permanently.
security.guard.branch_delete: Deleting a branch can discard commits that exist nowhere else.
security.guard.amend: Amending a published commit rewrites shared history.
security.guard.no_verify: --no-verify skips the hooks that protect this repository.
security.guard.suggest_force_with_lease: Prefer --force-with-lease: it refuses to overwrite commits you have not seen.
security.guard.approval_rejected: You rejected this operation, so it stays refused.
security.guard.approval_cancelled: The approval question for this operation was cancelled, so it was refused.
security.guard.approval_unavailable: This operation needs approval, but no approval channel is available, so it was refused.
security.sensitive_file_blocked: This call names a sensitive file, so it was not run: {file} (matched `{rule}`). Read the value from the environment, or ask the user to paste what is needed instead of the whole file.
security.secret_detected: This call carries what looks like a live credential, so it was not run. The value was not logged and is not repeated here.
security.secret_pattern_matched: Pattern matched: {pattern}. Rotate the credential if it has already been sent anywhere, and keep it in the environment or a secret store rather than in a prompt, a source file, or a command.
audit.enabled: Security audit enabled. Guard decisions are appended to {path}, which stays out of version control and out of the model's context.
audit.disabled: Security audit disabled. Guard decisions are no longer recorded, so a reviewer has no trail after the session ends.
trigger.pre_commit.detected: Checking this commit against the project workflow rules.
trigger.pre_commit.reason:
This commit breaks the project workflow rules.
{details}
trigger.pre_pr.detected: Checking this pull request against the project workflow rules.
trigger.pre_pr.reason:
This pull request breaks the project workflow rules.
{details}
trigger.pre_pr.error.description: The pull request description is missing a section the template asks for: {sections}. Say what changed, why, and how to verify it.
trigger.pre_pr.error.checklist: The pull request description leaves {count} checklist item(s) unticked. Tick each one, or delete the line if it does not apply.
trigger.pre_pr.warn.issue: The pull request names no issue. Reference one (`Closes #12`) when an issue exists, so the change can be traced back to its reason.
trigger.pre_release.detected: Checking this release against the project workflow rules.
trigger.pre_release.reason:
This release breaks the project workflow rules.
{details}
trigger.pre_release.error.version: `{version}` is not a semantic version. Use `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, optionally with a pre-release suffix such as `-rc.1`.
trigger.pre_release.error.version_mismat: The tag says `{tag}` but package.json says `{version}`. The tag and the published artefact must name the same version.
trigger.pre_release.error.prerelease_tag: `{version}` is a pre-release, so it must not be published to `latest`. Publish it with `--tag next`.
trigger.pre_release.error.changelog: The changelog has no `## [Unreleased]` section. Keep a Changelog keeps one at the top, and it is the section a release is cut from.
trigger.pre_release.error.changelog_cate: `### {section}` is not a Keep a Changelog category. Use Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, or Security.
trigger.pre_release.error.changelog_empt: The changelog has no entries for {version}. Write them under `[Unreleased]`, or move them into the `[{version}]` section when you cut the release.
skill.summary: Project workflow conventions are available as a skill. Read it before committing, branching, or changing documentation.
